item.title: After the ‘ceasefire’, the global silence – a message from Gaza
item.description: Gaza is treated as a temporary humanitarian problem rather than a long-term political failure requiring accountability, protection, and reconstruction. Once the violence becomes less visible, so does the obligation to act, writes Mahmoud Shehada in Gaza.

item.title: US Republicans accuse the EU of ‘decade-long censorship campaign’
item.description: In a fresh effort to recast regulation as censorship, a new 160-page report from the US House Judiciary Committee alleges Brussels pressured Big Tech platforms to censor US speech, including around the 2024 presidential elections.

item.title: Euro NCAP: Making car safety work for drivers, not against them
item.description: As of 2026, Euro NCAP (the European New Car Assessment Programme) is introducing its new and improved safety rating system for passenger cars — the largest revision since the introduction of the overall rating scheme in 2009.

item.title: EU pushes for partnership with US at Rubio-hosted critical minerals summit to counter China
item.description: Officials from the EU, US and around 50 countries are set to sign a joint 'framework' on critical minerals co-operation at the summit in Washington hosted by Marco Rubio.

item.title: Listen: What can the EU do about Israel’s violation of the peace plan in Gaza?
item.description: The EU welcomed the reopening of the Rafah crossing between Gaza and Egypt earlier this week. Meanwhile, Israeli authorities are blocking many NGOs from delivering humanitarian aid in Gaza, raising concerns over violations of the agreed peace plan. Will the EU take a stand on these human rights breaches?

item.title: Critics blame Greek coast guard tactics for migrant sea interception that left 15 dead
item.description: Greek authorities are facing criticism for launching an interception operation rather than a rescue mission for migrants stranded on a raft near a Greek island, after more than a dozen people were killed when their vessel collided with a high-speed patrol boat.

item.title: Major ‘reset’ coming on how EU Commission delivers humanitarian aid
item.description: The EU Commission will table a blueprint on humanitarian aid reform later this year, amid growing concern that the traditional model of development aid is now in its death throes. “The humanitarian system is going through a reset,” a commission spokesperson told reporters in Brussels on Wednesday (4 February). She added that the commission’s paper would be published […]

item.title: EU parliament trade committee edges closer to ratifying EU-US deal
item.description: “We must set clear boundaries and be ready to freeze negotiations or the application," said S&D trade committee chair Bernd Lange

item.title: Out of the cold: Growing number of EU capitals seek talks with Russia
item.description: The move would de facto end Russian president Vladimir Putin's diplomatic isolation by the West over his full invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Revealed: How Big Tech is lobbying on forthcoming EU Digital Fairness Act
item.description: New research by the Brussels NGO Corporate Europe Observatory (CEO) details an intense lobbying campaign by Big Tech to weaken the upcoming EU Digital Fairness Act — a proposal that aims to protect consumers from deceptive or addictive online features.
